approved: Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (News Media Diversity) Bill 2013
Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

Moved the Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (News Media Diversity) Bill 2013, arguing that a public interest test administered by an independent Public Interest Media Advocate would prevent transactions causing a substantial lessening of news diversity and support a strong, independent media sector.

Moved the Public Interest Media Advocate Bill 2013, proposing an independent statutory office to decide news media diversity transactions, assess self-regulatory schemes and complaints processes, and operate without ministerial or government direction.

Held up the 74-page Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (News Media Diversity) Bill and its 52-page explanatory memorandum, questioning how many government members voting on it had actually read either document, and likened the parliamentary chaos to the state of national debt heading past $260 billion.
Rose unexpectedly to speak, citing the confusion and chaos surrounding the government's handling of the media bills that evening.

Argued that the Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (News Media Diversity) Bill 2013 was intended to preserve a broad range of voices and prevent further concentration of news and commentary ownership, which was necessary for a healthy democracy.

Argued Australia's media ownership is dangerously concentrated, noting two companies control 86 per cent of the Australian newspaper market compared with 54 per cent in Canada and just 14 per cent in the United States, and pointed to Ireland's Press Council reforms as a model that went further than this bill proposes.

Supported the media diversity bill, arguing declining newspaper advertising revenue, down to around 10 cents online for every dollar once earned in print, has driven job losses across news organisations, and said protecting diversity matters because more than 80 per cent of Australian news is provided by just two entities.

Criticised the unusually shrill and substance-free public debate over the Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (News Media Diversity) Bill, saying in 15 years in parliament he had never seen legislation reported so hysterically, and set out to explain what the bill actually does.
